\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಕಳಿಸು} (kaḷisu)}{ಕಳಿಸು (kaḷisu)}]{\kn{ಕಳಿಸು} (kaḷisu) — to send}

\label{lesson:KA-C148-kalisu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to cut, then the Kannada for to break.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕಳಿಸು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕಳಿಸು}} — \emph{kaḷisu} — \textquotedblleft{}to send\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಕಳಿಸು}} (\emph{kaḷisu}) is native Dravidian, the verb that DEDR 1356 lists as Kannada \emph{kaḷe}, \emph{kaḷi}, \textquotedblleft{}to send forth, abandon, spend (time)\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-isu}, the ending that makes a verb \textquotedblleft{}cause to\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
